judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Exclusion 13(a)'s list of agents and representatives and with the Employee definition, requiring careful harmonisation across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph (a) ends with "or other similar representative" after a list of agents and contractors — an ejusdem generis question — and (b)(iii)'s sixty-day post-termination cut-off is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its representative list sits alongside Exclusion 12(n)'s "authorized representative" and the Employee definition; the three must be read together but do not contradict.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 13. Exclusions applicable to Insuring Clause 1 or 9

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Both limbs are stated by reference to defined terms and a specific carrier carve-out; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the boundary between Insuring Clauses 2/3 and Clauses 4–8, consistent with Exclusion 12(m).
judgments.clause_name: Crime 14. Exclusions applicable to Insuring Clause 2 or 3

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(as distinct from Robbery)" marks the line clearly, and the threat categories are specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Robbery definition and with the separate Kidnap/Ransom coverage section listed in the Schedule of Forms.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 15. Exclusion — kidnap, ransom or extortion payments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confined to registered or coupon obligations issued by an Insured; a narrow, determinate exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the Financial Instrument definition and Insuring Clause 4 without conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 16. Exclusion — registered or coupon obligations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sixty-day awareness trigger is objective, though "an Organization becomes aware" leaves the relevant knowledge-holder unspecified compared with the Discovery definition's Executive/Insurance Representative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Endorsement No. 4 deletes Exclusion 17 in its entirety, so this printed text is inoperative — a reader confronting the policy as issued must reconcile the two.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 17. Exclusion — Computer Fraud after awareness

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion of "any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument" is drafted in terms that mirror the very definition of Credit Card Fraud, an internal oddity, though the two provisos rescue coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Insuring Clause 8 and the Credit Card Fraud definition, the exclusion nearly consumes the grant unless the provisos are given work — a whole-instrument tension.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 18. Exclusion — credit card written instrument forgery

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three limbs are repetitive but each states sustained-before-termination plus discovery and notice within sixty days in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3(1) rewrites Exclusion 19 to a sustained-and-discovered-before-termination test with no sixty-day tail, while Endorsement No. 5 rewrites it with the sixty-day tail; both bear the same effective date and both purport to replace it in its entirety.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 19. Exclusion — loss sustained and discovered before termination

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Held by the Organization in any capacity whether or not the Organization is liable" is broad but standard bailment language, and the provisos are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It covers Insuring Clauses 1 through 8 and separately Clause 9, leaving Clause 10 unaddressed, but Clause 10 concerns expenses rather than property; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment to Insuring Clause 1 and the word-substitution instruction are stated with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs deletion of "sixty (60) days" from Exclusion 19, but Endorsement No. 3's version of Exclusion 19 contains no such words, so the substitution has nothing to operate on under one of the two competing endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable court costs and attorneys' fees" with a prior-consent requirement and two identified proceedings; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-referenced by Exclusion 12(i) and by Subsection 27's suit-limitation provision, both consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ten percent revenue test, sixty-day notice window and null-and-void consequence are all specific; "sole discretion" is broad but expressly conferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3(2) replaces the first paragraph of this subsection with a discovery-based trigger, so the printed opening no longer governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The four lettered conditions and the maximum-liability rule are set out with care and no obvious ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3(3) deletes this subsection in its entirety and all references to it, yet Subsection 25 still opens "Subject to Subsection 24" in the printed text — the deletion clause purports to cure that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause-by-clause single-loss aggregation rules are repetitive but precise, though "series of related acts" and "concerned or implicated" are terms that can require construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening words "Subject to Subsection 24" refer to a subsection deleted by Endorsement No. 3(3), and the first paragraph is itself replaced by Endorsement No. 3(4) with a discovery-based trigger that differs from the printed sustained-during-Policy-Period rule.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 25. Limits of Liability and Retention

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear anti-stacking rules with no soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Subsection 25's single-limit rules and the General Terms' separate-limits provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Earliest practicable moment" alongside hard ninety-day and six-month outer limits is a familiar formulation; the inventory-comparison restriction is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The condition-precedent notice duty is softened by Endorsement/Rider No. 1's prejudice rule and by General Terms Subsection 5's excuse clause, but the endorsement speaks only of a "Claim," leaving the interaction with this loss-notice duty unsettled.
judgments.clause_name: Crime 27. Proof of Loss and Legal Proceedings

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each measure of recovery is specified with a dated valuation source; "Lost Instrument Bond" is capitalised but undefined, a minor drafting slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the General Terms valuation provision, which yields to the coverage section, and with the Discovery definition's timing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-step waterfall stated in fixed order with a reinsurance carve-out; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the subrogation provision in the General Terms and with the retention structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Null and void to the extent of the amount recoverable or received" is awkward phrasing for an excess clause, and "recoverable" versus "received" could be read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(m)'s proviso uses the same excess concept, and the two are consistent in effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise amendment adding "trustee" to a lettered subparagraph; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cleanly supersedes the printed Executive definition in Subsection 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion instruction identifying the exclusion precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Exclusion 12(b) while the printed policy text still displays it, and the replacement privacy exclusion in the same endorsement is broader; the interaction is deliberate.
judgments.clause_name: Crime Endorsement/Rider No. 2 — deletion of Exclusion 12.(b)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Loss involving the disclosure ... or the use of another entity or person's confidential or personal information" plus "any similar type of nonpublic information" is a sweeping catch-all after a specific list, and "involving" is notably elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The proviso preserves only Insuring Clause 6, which raises the question whether the exclusion bites on losses otherwise covered by the Computer Fraud grant in Insuring Clause 5 — a live interaction with the coverage grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard heading and savings boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of the endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text is short and definite: loss must be both sustained and Discovered before termination, with no post-termination discovery window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5, effective the same date, also amends Exclusion 19 "in its entirety" and grants a sixty-day post-termination discovery and notice window — the two replacements cannot both be the operative Exclusion 19.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amended paragraph states a clear discovery-based trigger for newly acquired subsidiaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the first paragraph of Subsection 23, whose remaining paragraphs still speak of coverage being "null and void from the date of such acquisition," which fits the amended trigger adequately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unambiguous deletion instruction extending to all cross-references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Subsection 24 and by its terms cures the dangling "Subject to Subsection 24" opening of Subsection 25, which Endorsement 3(4) also rewrites — coherent as a package.
judgments.clause_name: Crime Endorsement No. 3 — (3) Deletion of Subsection 24

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence with two clear conditions: sustained before termination and Discovered during the Policy Period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This discovery-based trigger sits with Endorsement 3(1)'s version of Exclusion 19 but is in tension with Endorsement No. 5's sixty-day post-termination discovery window, which would allow coverage for loss discovered after the Policy Period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate with no operative content.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 17 remains printed in the coverage section, so the policy as issued must be read with this deletion in mind, but the instruction is unambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text restates the sixty-day discovery-and-notice tail with three parallel limbs; the wording itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to replace Exclusion 19 in its entirety, as does Endorsement No. 3(1) with materially different content and the same effective date, and it also sits against Endorsement 3(4)'s requirement that loss be Discovered during the Policy Period.
